audit_question.question: When handleAcceptReply consumes F3, can recovery or retry retain acceptance counts or reuse a ballot while instance commands change, allowing a delayed guarded-no-op report to support commitment of commands its sender did not accept?
audit_question.importance: If historical ballot reports are counted as acceptance of different current commands, the replica could mark unsupported commands COMMITTED, broadcast that marker, and issue successful client replies. Neither a legal witness nor that consequence has yet been established.
objects: Instance cmds, bal, vbal, status and lb
Replica Id, N, defaultBallot and maxRecvBallot
contexts: In-memory processing with delayed protocol replies
Repeated recovery of an existing instance
Prepare-reply transitions interleaved with acceptance reports and full Commit reconciliation
Crash persistence excluded from the immediate discriminator
Participant initialization, quorum configuration and transport legality remain unresolved
event_paths: New initializes maxRecvBallot, smallestDefaultBallot and every defaultBallot entry to -1; participant identity and quorum configuration are delegated to replica.New.
recover allocates bookkeeping only when absent, retaining existing counters and client proposals otherwise.
makeBallot assigns lastTriedBallot without resetting counters and permits equality with the current bounds.
handleCommit can replace commands and clear clientProposals while retaining bookkeeping; handlePrepareReply can subsequently assign proposal commands or NOOP without a committed-state guard.
handleAccept reports the current instance ballot even when its lower-ballot or committed-state guard prevents command installation.
handleAcceptReply filters by current status and lastTriedBallot, then increments acceptOKs and may commit current commands.
counterevidence: For an unchanged attempt, rejection of a lower outgoing ballot reports a higher ballot and follows the consumer's nack branch.
Missing-instance and ordinary accepted branches install incoming commands and ballot before replying.
handleAcceptReply discards lower-ballot reports and returns while the local instance is COMMITTED.
handlePrepare sends a full Commit for a committed instance; whether reconciliation necessarily precedes ambiguous reply consumption remains unresolved.
run serializes protocol handlers and recovery dispatch, excluding simultaneous handler execution but allowing delayed-message interleavings.
handlePropose creates fresh bookkeeping with zero counters; retained counters concern existing-instance recovery and retries.

Repeated prepare-reply threshold transitions reconstruct the same commands while clientProposals remains unchanged. Counter retention or ballot reuse alone therefore does not establish command substitution.
makeBallot starts at Id and advances by N for leaders. Unique participant identities may constrain ballot ownership, but the embedded initialization and legal message histories remain unverified.
Full Commit reconciliation sets COMMITTED, which blocks AcceptReply consumption until another reachable transition changes that status.
unknowns: A legal same-instance history connecting command replacement, retained counters, and a matching delayed guarded-no-op report.

The reachable effect of handleAcceptReply passing areply.Ballot to makeBallot, whose argument indexes instanceSpace; the target may be another initialized instance or may cause failure before retry.
The applicable contract for treating matching ballot reports and implicit local support as sufficient acceptance of current commands.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The acquired constructor and declarations resolve field order and initial ballot values: both proposal and recovery bookkeeping start with zero counters, and existing recovery bookkeeping is retained. They do not establish participant identity or transport semantics because those responsibilities lie in the embedded replica implementation. The discriminator now requires a legal command-changing history, not merely repeated counters or equal ballots.

selection_rationale: Continue the same F3 consumption question. Initialization confirms the retained-counter interpretation but does not prove that a matching historical report can support different commands. The cross-path comparison identifies full Commit processing as a concrete command/proposal-changing path, with committed-state filtering as relevant counterevidence. Read the embedded initialization, quorum helpers and send implementation before deriving a contract or constructing a legal schedule. The completed constructor request has been removed. No new source-grounded inventory correction is required by this review; candidate-specific path composition remains on the question.
